title: I Posted the Apartment Package Photo the Lobby Camera Already Had

parts.text: I watched my box walk out the lobby in someone else's hands. I am thirty-three, IT, lunch break, phone in hand. The hands belonged to my neighbor Chris from 4B, cheerful, always in a college hoodie. The box was cat litter, embarrassing, heavy, mine. The lobby smelled like wet umbrellas. The manager, Fay, had said cameras were dummy globes. Chris said, "I thought it was a misdeliver" I said, "It has my name in two places" I asked Fay for the clip anyway. She stalled. I can still name the ugly little detail, which is how I know it happened. I noticed a scuff on the floor shaped like a comma, which fit i. Someone had left a receipt in the cup holder, faded blue ink. The air tasted like leftover rain and cleaning spray, which fit i. A cheap clock on the wall jumped a minute late, then caught up. I kept my keys in my left pocket so I would not fidget, which fit i. The plastic chair stuck to my legs when I shifted. A vending machine hummed in another room like a bored insect, which fit i. I counted three ceiling tiles with water stains before I spoke again. My socks had a hole I had been ignoring since Tuesday, which fit i.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: He still has the box in the elevator, and Fay is calling the cameras fake.

parts.text: I rode the next elevator and knocked on 4B with Fay on speaker. Chris opened, litter box in the hall like a confession. He said he was going to bring it later. Later is a long word. Fay admitted the globes record to a cheap cloud she hates logging into. She logged in. The clip was ugly and clear. Chris offered to Venmo a late fee he invented. I took the litter and a written note on the package shelf: names face up, cameras real. He avoids the lobby when I get mail. The cats were unimpressed, which is correct. Fay said, "Please don't post the video" I said, "Then post the sign" The umbrella smell is seasonal. The hoodie is still in the clip.
